content.text:
I made `0.svg` into the digit 0. The file was empty: just `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"/>`, with no shapes, `viewBox` or size. It drew nothing, so there was no artwork to improve. The filename was the only clue, so I took it to mean a zero:

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2">
  <rect x="7" y="3" width="10" height="18" rx="5"/>
</svg>
```

- **`viewBox` plus 24×24 size:** it scales cleanly and has a sensible default size wherever you use it.
- **`currentColor` stroke:** the zero takes on the color of the text around it, the same way Lucide and Tabler icons work.
- **Whole-pixel edges:** the edges of the outline fall on whole pixels, so it looks sharp at 24px.

I couldn't check it with a tool. Both commands I tried were blocked because this session can't approve them: one to find an SVG renderer so I could preview it, and `xmllint` to confirm it's valid XML. I checked the shape's coordinates by hand instead.

If "0" is just a file number and you meant something else, tell me what it should show. The original was the single line quoted above. If the file was supposed to have artwork already, whatever created it probably saved an empty file.
